basis: Macroglossia, hyperinsulinism and lateralized skeletal overgrowth/abdominal-wall defects are defining BWS features; tumour predisposition is a risk.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: hyperinsulinism is a major BWS diagnostic criterion; transient neonatal hypoglycemia alone would not suffice.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: lateralized skeletal overgrowth and abdominal-wall defects are major structural features, rather than generalized large size alone.

basis: Platelet defect and vision-impairing albinism define HPS9; immune dysfunction has leukopenia/infections in 1/1. Cutaneous hypopigmentation is a core, usually common feature; primary cap applies.

decisions.ocular: primary: ocular albinism with reduced acuity and nystagmus is defining; ocular albinism is reported in 1/1.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: cutaneous hypopigmentation is part of the core albinism phenotype, expected in >=30%; the three primary slots prioritize blood, vision and immune dysfunction.
decisions.infectious_immune: primary: leukopenia and recurrent infections in 1/1, together with inborn-immunity ancestry, support an immunodeficiency mechanism.

basis: Tumour arises in brain, spinal cord or meninges. Endothelial differentiation alone does not establish separate cardiovascular organ disease.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: vascular histology describes tumour lineage; the affected organ is CNS, without demonstrated separate heart or vessel disease.

basis: Inherited coagulation disorder; thromboembolism is a separately diagnosed complication, with no supplied >=30% frequency. Osteonecrosis ancestry alone is insufficient.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: thrombophilia is a coagulation disorder; thromboembolism is a separately coded complication and its frequency is unspecified.

basis: Treponemal infection defined by skin and oral mucosal lesions. Destructive bone disease is variable; involvement in >=30% is not established.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: oral mucosal lesions are characteristic defining manifestations of bejel; mouth belongs to gastrointestinal.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: periostitis and late bone destruction can occur, but a >=30% frequency or required diagnostic status is not established.

basis: The supplied definition includes developmental disability, congenital cardiac abnormalities and renal hypoplasia among the syndrome's defining structural features.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: congenital cardiac abnormalities, including patent ductus arteriosus, are explicitly part of the defining phenotype.
decisions.renal: primary: renal hypoplasia is explicitly included in the syndrome definition; genital abnormalities alone would not establish this axis.

basis: Clonal mast-cell proliferation infiltrates and damages skin. Mediator-related diarrhea and hypotension do not establish extracutaneous damage; marrow abnormalities are only 1-4%.

decisions.haematologic: primary: mastocytosis is a proliferative disease of hematopoietic mast cells; a blood-cell neoplasm need not occupy marrow to qualify.

basis: Retinal dystrophy 7/8, obesity 8/8 and polydactyly 8/8 are defining features. Neurologic impairment: intellectual disability 3/3 and developmental delay 5/7. Renal frequency unestablished.

decisions.neurologic: involved: intellectual disability in 3/3 and developmental delay in 5/7 establish common functional damage; three primary slots hold core diagnostic features.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: polydactyly is a major BBS diagnostic feature and occurs in 8/8 reported subtype patients.

basis: Cardiac malformations, strabismus and urethral hypospadias each occur in 30-79%. Dental abnormalities (30-79%) omitted at the four-axis cap; their functional severity is unspecified.

decisions.renal: involved: hypospadias is a structural urethral defect reported in 30-79%; urethra is explicitly within this axis.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: dental abnormalities occur in 30-79%, but are omitted at cap; unspecified dental severity ranks below cardiac, ocular and urethral structural dysfunction.

basis: Supplied HPO: bleeding, pyloric stenosis and scoliosis each 80-99%; definition supports coagulopathy. Cardiac defects (30-79%) omitted at cap; frequencies may overrepresent syndromic forms.

decisions.haematologic: involved: abnormal bleeding is annotated 80-99%, and the definition identifies coagulopathy; supplied evidence supports a common hematologic manifestation.
decisions.cardiovascular: none: omitted at cap; ductal and valve defects are annotated 30-79%, while retained extracerebral manifestations each have supplied 80-99% frequencies.
